key_insight: AI-integrated blood profiling linked MFAT treatment to molecular patterns consistent with cartilage protection and reduced inflammation, distinct from those following hyaluronic acid.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest potential disease-modifying effects in knee osteoarthritis, but blood molecular signatures alone do not establish disease modification.
method: Analysed samples from a double-blind randomised trial comparing MFAT with hyaluronic acid.
Integrated plasma proteomics, N-glycomics, miRNA profiles, genetics and molecular networks using interpretable non-negative matrix tri-factorisation.
Tracked molecular patterns at baseline, one month and six months.
evidence_signal: The analysis resolved 93 gene and 30 miRNA pathways, with distinct six-month treatment signatures accompanying reported MFAT advantages in pain, function and cartilage composition.
watch_item: The abstract omits sample size and effect sizes; independent validation and longer-term structural outcomes are needed to substantiate disease modification.
paper_title: Micro-fragmented adipose tissue reprogrammes the systemic molecular landscape of inflammatory knee osteoarthritis
